title: AXI4-to-AHB5 Bridge Obligations
description: Trace accepted AXI4 requests through buffered AW-order association, 4 KB-to-1 KB burst splitting, serialized AHB phases, and ID-aware response reconstruction without equating lock, exclusive, protection, or security mechanisms.

annotations.message: The bridge can advertise only the outstanding depth it can preserve. It retains full ID and request context; accepting W before AW requires storage until an accepted AW assigns that data in AXI4 write-address order.
An AXI burst that obeys its 4 KB rule can still cross an AHB 1 KB boundary. The bridge derives addresses and splits the downstream work so every emitted AHB burst remains inside one 1 KB region.

AHB reports completion per transfer, while AXI returns RRESP per read beat and one BRESP per write transaction. The bridge preserves BID/RID context and applies its documented error aggregation and mapping.
AHB address ownership and data/response ownership remain phase-aware. Serialization, arbitration, and service limits are bridge or system policy, not new AXI protocol rules.

Protection and security attributes require an explicit supported mapping, such as appropriate AxPROT information into HPROT/HNONSEC. AxCACHE, AxQOS, and AxREGION have no universal one-to-one AHB encoding.

A downstream AHB ERROR is normally surfaced as AXI SLVERR; an upstream decode miss can produce DECERR. The bridge must document the exact mapping and cannot return OKAY after an observed downstream error.

AXI exclusive access, original-AHB locking, AHB5 HMASTLOCK, AHB5 exclusive signaling, and security attribution are distinct. A bridge maps only mechanisms it implements and otherwise rejects or degrades them according to an explicit contract.
